description: Pinned descriptor of the Claude Code hook-output contract the Enforcement Canary validates against. A control that 'blocks' in a shape Claude Code ignores is a silent no-op: the hook believes it denied, the tool call proceeds. Tier 1 validates each control's emitted output against THIS pin. Re-validate the pin on every Claude Code upgrade (platform-drift guard) — a stale pin turns healthy installs red.

PreToolUse.exitCodeDenyNote: Claude Code honors exit code 2 (with stderr) as a PreToolUse block — the legacy 'blocking error' contract. This is how MOST 0K-Talon controls block (L0, L1 Governor, gh-policy, L9): they do NOT emit a JSON envelope. A block is HONORED if EITHER exit==2 OR a valid hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny. The silent-no-op class is specifically exit==0 AND a decision Claude Code ignores (top-level decision/tool_input). A crash (non-zero exit that is NOT 2, with no decision) is an ERROR, not a block.

deadFormatSignals.description: Top-level shapes Claude Code IGNORES at exit 0. If a hook emits one of these AND exits 0 (does not use exit-code-2 either), its block is a silent no-op.
